task:
Build a Python module named textkit with three functions:

1. word_count(text: str) -> int
   Count words. A word is a maximal run of letters or digits.
   "hello, world" has 2 words. "hello,world" has 2 words. "one-two" has 2 words.

2. unique_words(text: str) -> list[str]
   Return unique words in first-seen order, compared case-insensitively, stored lowercase.
   "One one TWO two Three" -> ["one", "two", "three"].

3. is_palindrome(text: str) -> bool
   True when the letters and digits read the same forward and backward.
   Ignore case, spaces, and punctuation.
   "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" -> True.
   "race a car" -> False.
plan: Ship one module, textkit.py, with three pure functions: word_count, unique_words, and is_palindrome. No network, no files, no extra dependencies. A word is a maximal run of letters or digits, so punctuation splits words and is not itself a word. Unique words are lowercase and keep first-seen order. A palindrome compares letters and digits only, ignoring case. test_textkit.py is the contract. It is frozen. The coder may not edit it.
acceptance_criteria: word_count counts maximal runs of letters or digits and treats punctuation as a separator.
unique_words returns lowercase words in first-seen order.
is_palindrome ignores case, spaces, and punctuation.
The coder may change textkit.py only.
Done means the frozen pytest suite exits 0.
